positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ADDRESS PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERNS ABOUT HUMAN VIRAL PATHOGENS IN TREATED WASTEWATER FOR NON-POTABLE REUSE ACROSS THE UNITED STATES. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE IDENTIFYING A SUITE OF VIRAL PATHOGENS AND SURROGATES AND DETECTION METHODS THAT MAY BEST SERVE AS AN INDICATION OF VIRAL RISK IN WATER REUSE. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE A LIST OF BEST METHODS FOR IDENTIFYING THE VIRAL RISK FOR NON-POTABLE WATER REUSE AND STANDARD OPERATING PROTOCOLS (SOPS) FOR THESE METHODS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE WASTEWATER OPERATORS, STATE AND LOCAL REGULATORS, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. THE UNIVERSITY OF MIAMI WILL PARTICIPATE IN WASTEWATER SAMPLE AND WATER QUALITY DATA COLLECTION. TULANE UNIVERSITY, THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII, UC DAVIS AND THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE CROSS-LABORATORY STUDY TO COMPARE METHODS FOR DETECTION OF SELECTIVE VIRAL PATHOGENS AND SURROGATES.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO EXPAND THE CURRENT UNDERSTANDING OF VIRUS FATE DURING WASTEWATER TREATMENT AND DEVELOP SURROGATE-BASED CREDITING FRAMEWORKS FOR UNIT PROCESSES THAT HAVE LARGELY BEEN UNCREDITED OR UNDER-CREDITED IN NONPOTABLE AND POTABLE REUSE APPLICATIONS. DELIVERABLES WILL ELUCIDATE POTENTIAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN CULTURE AND MOLECULAR DATA FOR HUMAN ENTERIC VIRUSES, SURROGATE BACTERIOPHAGES, AND FECAL INDICATOR VIRUSES. OUTCOMES OF THE RESEARCH INCLUDE SURROGATE-BASED PREDICTIVE MODELS AND REGULATORY CREDITING FRAMEWORKS THAT CAN BE READILY ADOPTED BY STATES AND THE WATER INDUSTRY. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE RESIDENTS OF COMMUNITIES IN NEVADA, VIRGINIA, AND FLORIDA SERVED BY CBAT FACILITIES COVERED BY THE STUDY, WASTEWATER OPERATORS, STATE AND LOCAL REGULATORS, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. SUBAWARDEE DREXEL UNIVERSITY WILL WORK ON MATHEMATICAL MODEL DEVELOPMENT.

DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A RATING OF EIGHT WASTEWATER TREATMENT PROCESSES WITH RESPECT TO REMOVALS/INACTIVATION OF HUMAN ENTERIC VIRUSES, AND DATA WITH THE OUTCOME OF ULTIMATELY INFORMING POLICIES AND GUIDELINES RELATIVE TO TESTING OF WASTEWATER TREATMENT TECHNOLOGIES BEING CONSIDERED FOR REUSE OF TREATED WASTEWATER. DESCRIPTION:THIS PROJECT AIMS TO EVALUATE THE RELATIVE IMPACTS OF PERCHLORATE FROM FIREWORKS ON SURFACE DRINKING WATER SOURCES AND GROUNDWATER DRINKING SOURCES ACROSS THE US BY MEASURING PERCHLORATE AT SIX SITES (TWO RIVERS, THREE LAKES, AND A GROUNDWATER SITE) DURING JULY 4TH EVENTS, AS WELL AS PERIODIC FIREWORK DISPLAYS FROM BASEBALL STADIUMS ON THE TWO RIVERS SELECTED. SEVEN SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES WILL BE ADDRESSED THROUGH A COMBINATION OF FIELD AND LABORATORY STUDIES COMBINED WITH MODELING EFFORTS TO FILL CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS.ACTIVITIES:DRINKING WATER SOURCES IN THE WATERSHEDS WILL BE EVALUATED BEFORE AND AFTER MAJOR PERIODS OF FIREWORKS AND DURING SUBSEQUENT RAIN EVENTS. IN ADDITION TO MEASURING THE PERCHLORATE INPUTS DUE TO RUNOFF OR INFILTRATION, THE RESEARCH WILL ALSO MEASURE THE DIRECT DEPOSITION INTO WATER BODIES. AERIAL DEPOSITION WILL BE MEASURED BY LIMITED DIRECT AIR AND DEPOSITION SAMPLING AT SOME SITES. TO EXPAND THE REACH OF THE STUDY, ADDITIONAL SAMPLES WILL BE REQUESTED FROM CASTNET AND NADP (TWO EXISTING SAMPLING NETWORKS), AND THE PROJECT WILL ALSO INCLUDE NATION-WIDE SURVEYS OF PUBLIC WATER SUPPLY INTAKES BEFORE AND AFTER PERIODS OF FIREWORKS. UNIVERSITY OF DELAWARE ($319,999): SUBAWARD FOR (1) SAMPLING THE MASSACHUSETTS LOCATION, AND (2) STABLE ISOTOPE ANALYSES (OBJECTIVES 4 AND 5). UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, LAS VEGAS ($329,985): SUBAWARD FOR (1) SAMPLING THE LAS VEGAS LOCATION, AND (2) STUDIES ON AIR DEPOSITION, CITIZEN SCIENTIST LAKE SURVEY, LAKE MODELING (OBJECTIVES 1, 2, AND 6).

ADDITIONAL OUTPUTS INCLUDE REFINED AND CALIBRATED MODELS TO EVALUATE PERCHLORATE INPUT AND FATE IN SURFACE WATER RESOURCES, A NATIONAL SURVEY OF THE IMPACT OF PERCHLORATE IN DRINKING WATER SOURCES, IDENTIFICATION OF KEY PREDICTIVE VARIABLES TO PREDICT PERCHLORATE IMPACT, AND DEVELOPMENT OF A SCREENING TOOL TO EVALUATE IMPACTS. POTENTIAL BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE DRINKING WATER UTILITIES AS WELL AS STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND COMMUNITIES WHOSE DRINKING WATER IS AFFECTED BY POLLUTION FROM THE USE OF FIREWORKS.
